Thank you for everything, Geraldine!","text_translated":"","published_at":"2024-11-16T01:44:33.95065Z"},{"Name":"Lisa ELam","ProfilePicture":"https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/a-/ALV-UjVDW0qpttPxg49ksiLAz-9gqKQVcT5zv99z8NReQSh21_Z-jMla=s120-c-rp-mo-ba12-br100","Rating":2,"Description":"Our wedding day was absolutely beautiful and calm thanks to Sharlene and Yaris. They truly worked hard to keep things organized, and I want to thank them for that. I also want to thank the lady who created the bouquets and boutonnieres because she did an incredible job. My bouquet was honestly one of the most beautiful I have ever seen.

However, I was disappointed with several things that were changed or mishandled without my consent. While I understand weather can cause adjustments, the setup I originally agreed to was not respected. The floral arch I chose was swapped for something completely different, and instead of lanterns on the ground as planned, there were open candles that guests had to move so my dress would not catch fire. It was stressful in the moment, but I stayed quiet to focus on enjoying my day.

The timeline also felt rushed. My wedding was supposed to end at 10:30 PM, yet by 9:30 PM almost everything was packed up and the night was essentially over. No guest table should be cleared until guests actually leave because it makes people feel like they need to go. Many did not even get cake, and parts of my three-tier cake went missing. The cake was made to serve 75 people, but by the time we cut it, fewer than 30 guests remained. On top of that, sentimental items including my late grandmother’s vase and a custom centerpiece my friend made were never returned. My friend confirmed she did not take hers home, so these were misplaced or taken by the planners, which is extremely upsetting.

When I later opened the top of my cake that I saved for our anniversary, I found they had picked the shells off of it. I cried. That cake was expensive and deeply sentimental, and seeing it altered after so many other things went missing truly broke my heart.

After the wedding, I spoke with Sharlene about my centerpieces, which were large hand-picked ocean shells I had paid for. She told me she offered them to guests, which I was never told would happen. I had 14 centerpieces but only five remained when I went to gift them to my family. These were irreplaceable keepsakes that cost hundreds of dollars, and they were treated like they meant nothing.

Throughout planning, communication with the main planner, Gerardine, became increasingly uncomfortable. After a disagreement with my mother, which I apologized for multiple times, her attitude toward me changed. I started feeling awkward and guilty even when making necessary changes such as moving the venue due to my parents’ health, which were beyond my control. Once we moved to the Hilton, their workload was lighter because the Hilton planners handled much of the logistics, yet I still felt like a burden.

There were also unprofessional money issues. We were supposed to be reimbursed for 70 chairs and cocktail tables that were not needed since the Hilton provided them. Instead, the planner rented a small car on the wedding day and charged us $200 to upgrade to a larger vehicle to move our items, effectively using our refund to cover her mistake.

Communication after the wedding was equally frustrating. When I asked about missing items, I was told my family should have helped them pack. When I questioned why my ceremony arch and walkway were not correct, I was given this response:
“Hi Lisa, Hi, we’re closing the chat at this time. All further updates and communication will continue via email.”
That was the end of it.

I truly hope this company takes this feedback seriously and improves its professionalism because Sharlene and Yaris have huge potential. Contractual Breaches & Lack of Professionalism: The company failed to adhere to the agreed-upon contract terms and made several unapproved design and technical changes on the wedding day. We strongly advise future clients to keep their signed contract readily available and to note that this company may not follow it.

Bride and Mother Assumed Planner Roles: We ended up completing several tasks that should have been managed by the wedding planners as part of their service. My daughter had to provide the seating chart to the staff multiple times prior to the day of the event.

Ignored Ceremony Design: The contract specified a desired ceremony design, which was completely ignored in favor of a different, unrequested look. Although the alternative design was lovely, it was not what the bride requested or paid for.

Post-Event Logistics and Missing Items: The lack of a plan for the collection and distribution of items at the end of the evening was a major disappointment. There was no company representative present to manage the materials, leaving the couple to deal with everything the next morning. Furthermore, several valuable items went missing:
*Centerpieces and Conch Shells: Expensive, specific conch shells fished from Sanibel Beach over months for the event and intended as gifts disappeared.
*Gifted Items: A flower spray gifted to the couple was also missing.

Wedding Cake Service: The $1,200 wedding cake, intended to serve 75 guests, was poorly served in tiny slivers to only some attendees. No one received any of the edible shells from the cake, and the whereabouts of the remaining cake and shells are unknown.

Blame Shifting: When confronted about the post-event issues, the company blamed the wedding couple for not having a family member present at the end to ensure proper distribution of materials. The purpose of hiring event planners is so the couple and their family can enjoy the day without managing logistics from start to finish. Additionally the company understood the Bride's parents were recovering from cancer and were physically unable to stay until the end of the evening.

This experience was highly stressful and disappointing. The venue itself is stunning, and the staff played an important role in making my special day come together.

Anabel, my wedding coordinator, was by far the best part of my experience. She was incredibly professional, responsive, and kind throughout the entire process. Anabel guided me through every detail, went above and beyond on the wedding day, and ensured everything was perfect. Her calm and supportive demeanor made all the difference, and I cannot thank her enough for the effort she put into making my day stress-free and magical.

At the beginning of the planning process, Aida, the manager I believe, was very helpful and nice. She assisted with many of the initial details and was kind in addressing questions I had early on. However, two weeks before the wedding, I was asked to provide my final guest count. I had originally paid for 130 guests, but my final count ended up being lower. I asked if the extra amount I paid could be applied to something else, like adding an extra hour to the event. Anabel kindly explained that because the proteins had already been ordered, they couldn’t accommodate the request.

Since I didn’t recall being told that my final headcount was due 30 days prior, I reached out to Aida to discuss the matter. Unfortunately, her response came across as rude and dismissive. When I explained my concerns, she said, “We don’t have to tell you.” I found this response unhelpful and inappropriate, especially so close to my wedding day. As a first-time bride, I was still learning how everything worked, and I expected more understanding and professionalism. Not per se to just magically make it work for me, I understood proteins were ordered nothing else we could do, but Aida’s response was what threw me. Additionally, the contract did not clearly specify the 30-day requirement, which made the situation more confusing. I chose to end the conversation there, as it wasn’t constructive.

Thankfully, Anabel stepped in and reassured me that all the food would be cooked and that guests could have seconds if they wanted. Her professionalism, kindness, and willingness to help stood out, and she worked tirelessly to ensure everything turned out beautifully.

One thing to note about The Vintage is that they are very strict about their contract. Be sure to read it carefully, section by section, before you sign it. If you’re a first-time bride, make sure to ask these important questions upfront:
•	How long before the ceremony can we come in to get ready?
•	How long is the rehearsal?
•	How long do we have to clean up afterward?
•	What isn’t included in this contract?
•	What setup does the venue include?
•	How many hours am I contracted for the venue?
•	When is my final headcount due?
•       How long before the wedding can I set up my decorations? (They will not set up your decorations outside, they do not offer this service)

Both E&M Sweet (cake), William Solozano(DJ/MC), and the wait staff exceeded our expectations, and we are so grateful for their contributions to our special day! The wait staff were attentive and ensured that my groom, bridal party, and I had the cocktail hour appetizers set aside for us to enjoy. If you’re planning your wedding at The Vintage, I highly recommend considering them as your vendors—you won’t be disappointed.

The vintage doesn’t include the alcohol which means you bring your own and can possibly save on the bar tab.

I worked with Ada from very early on and she was very accommodating. She answered all my questions in a timely manner and also made sure that my day was very smooth and it was! Everything felt very smooth!

Some things I want to point out that helped my experience: they lowered the minimum guest count for me and also adjusted it for me twice when I realized I had made a mistake in my numbers. They also were VERY accommodating when my husband and I decided to move up our wedding 4 months early. The change fee is only $500, which I think is very reasonable! Huge thank you for that! Also, the venue prepares a sampler plate for the bride and groom from the cocktail hour and it’s so awesome (and delicious).

The bartender was also very nice! I’m sure this depends on the day, but the blonde Argentinian lady we had was so sweet.

Lastly,  the bridal and groom suite are really nice to have so I would definitely add these to your package!

Something to consider, and the reason I give 4 stars and not 5, and this is meant to be constructive feedback for the business owners so they can consider and hopefully  improve:
1) I honestly felt really pressured to book this place in the early stage and I didn’t like that experience at all. It made me feel uneasy and silly. Luckily it was a beautiful space that we wanted and was meant for us. Advise for the company: let the beauty of the place speak for itself and don’t pressure anyone to submit a deposit. A wedding venue is a huge decision and shouldn’t be taken lightly and it would feel more authentic if this sentiment came through. Advise for couples (and this is for any venue you book): take your time. It’s your day and you deserve the time to decide in peace :)
2. The vintage will not decorate for you. Ada was very transparent about this. They put up table signs and helped put out our favors on the table but you’re on your own for outdooor decor. Advice for future couples: tell Ada (or whoever you work with) early on who is decorating outside and if there is glass involved. Advice for the business: consider changing this and including it in the package. To be considered “all-inclusive” I think setting up outdoor decor should be included and the responsibility of the venue.
3. The preferred florist vendor provided to us was Natinel Flowers and due to their high praise from the vintage, we decided to book with them and had a horrendous experience. The florist was unprofessional, unorganized, and not transparent about costs (ex. tried to charge me more for my bridal bouquet the DAY before my wedding even though I asked for the style before paying and it was noted in the invoice). Advise for couple: find another florist. Advise to the business: do not recommend this florist. She adds a lot of unnecessary stress to the bride and groom.

In general… I planned very carefully and was in constant communication with Ada which I felt resulted in a smooth and wonderful wedding day. I couldn’t have dreamt of a better experience honestly. Big thank you to Ada and your team for making this day so special!

My husband and I got engaged in June 2024 and married two years later in June 2026 in New York City. We found Rachel in August 2024, signed her on immediately after our initial chat, allowing us to work together for 22 months. Start to finish, it was one of the most special experiences of my entire life. Rachel extended the ‘wedding highs’ throughout every part of the process, from venue tours to going to pick out linens and tableware, to our tasting and our floral and decor mock up. We felt so supported and well cared for along the way, but I want to emphasize how much fun we had together with Rachel and the incredible network of vendors she extended to us.

I work in branding, have a specific vision, and certainly like to do things ‘my way’ and rather than making me ever feel difficult, Rachel only encouraged and ran with the big plans or found the most creative solutions to my strange asks. My husband did not have a specific vision, was along for the ride, but I’d be remiss if I didn’t mention the passion and creativity Rachel pulled out of him. It was incredible to see how inspired he was by all the event planning efforts, and by the end, he ended up planning the after party (props and all…) It was a super sweet bonding experience for us.

I say this because whether you’re all in on the planning process or just along for the ride, I’m confident Rachel and team will always meet you where you’re at and steer the ship that only gets heavier as guests, plans, finances, etc. tack on.

And lastly!!! I want to talk about how perfectly our wedding weekend went. Tuesday afternoon her team started picking up all our packed wedding supplies from our apartment. Sunday morning, post wedding, our stuff was waiting for us back at our apartment. I had some dress issues, the usual stuff you can’t avoid, and Rachel and her team were there for it all with multiple solutions prepared. AND kept the energy calm, positive and cheerful. Never stressed or rushed. Every team member I interacted with was kind, polished and professional, of course, but I genuinely felt cared for and loved by them as if they were who I had been working with all 22 months! I was lucky to be able to work with Lizzie throughout the process as well and it feels extra special when another full time planner is as tapped into your wedding as one of her own.

Planning a wedding during the school year for two teachers in less than a year is no easy feat! We knew that we needed help. The moment we met Brittney on Zoom we knew that we would be in the best of hands. Her calm demeanor, her balance of organization and fun - but, we also felt that she “got us” as a couple. She understood us and our unique dream of having a small ceremony with a fantastic, big party.

Working with Brittney and Kiersten was seamless. Brittney helped us focus in on our two locations (ceremony and dinner + reception) by connecting us with amazing vendors and venues in our beloved Brooklyn. Both Brittney and Kiersten actively listened to us and picked up on details that showed up in all of our visits and Zoom calls with said vendors. (Shout out to @justinjunleeweddings @forgedinthenorth @willowhousebeauty @fernbotanica - we love you all!) All of the vendors we worked with were all recommended by Brittney and her team - and, they were all so lovely to work with. We were in the best of hands across the board, all thanks to Brittney. We kept saying that we had the best team! (Go #team!)

Leading up to the weekend, Brittney and Kiersten checked in with us every step of the way, from email messages with reminders, to quick calls to iron out details. We also so appreciated a final Zoom call with all of our vendors before the big day. Brittney was so organized and led our call with a smile. It was really great to be with all of our vendors at one time and to hear all of the care and planning that each had given to our preparations. We felt so ready.

Our wedding weekend was all that we hoped for. We were able to focus on being with each other as a couple and bask in the glow of our love and all of our loved ones. Brittney and Kiersten (and all of our vendors!) were able to execute all of the plans, as well as stopping by to check in on us as we got ready, keeping us posted and checking to see if we needed anything.  It wasn’t lost on us that our three-day celebration asked Brittney and Kiersten to be “in it” for the entire weekend. They were so patient and calm - and always ready to smile and laugh with us. We kept saying, “Wait, we don’t want to be done! We are going to miss them!”

And, it’s true. We felt so cared for and the trust we have in Brittney is unmatched. She is so knowledgeable when it comes to wedding planning and vendor matching. The comfort and care she gave us and our families was so appreciated and we would recommend BLB to anyone who is planning their special day - or in our case - days!

These are just a few of the many issues we dealt with throughout the process.

Just 26 days before our wedding, after 11 months of planning around a 5:00 PM to 1:00 AM open bar, Karen (the owner/operator) told us she was no longer okay with the timeline she'd known about from the very beginning. There wasn't a licensing issue or a staffing issue. She simply decided that eight hours of bar service was "too much."

We suddenly had to choose between serving cocktails during cocktail hour or having drinks at our after-party, even though we'd already paid $2,500 for the Speakeasy specifically for that purpose. We even offered to cancel the Speakeasy and either receive a refund or apply the $2,500 toward our bar package. Instead of having a reasonable conversation, Karen threatened to get her lawyers involved.

From there, we were left scrambling to find another after-party venue less than a month before the wedding, while still paying for vendors like our DJ and photographer whose schedules had already been built around the original timeline. There was no way to recover those costs. One last-minute decision ended up costing us thousands of dollars.

Another moment that perfectly sums up what it was like working with Karen happened the night before our wedding. We had requested Bud Light be added to our beverage package a full year earlier, and it had already been approved, invoiced, and paid for. Then, while we were at our rehearsal dinner, Karen emailed saying she had misquoted the price and that we now owed $200 immediately instead of the $45 we'd already paid, or the beer would be returned.

It wasn't about the $200. It was the timing. Who creates a last-minute issue the night before someone's wedding over something that had been settled weeks earlier? And frankly, $200 for two cases of Bud Light is ridiculous.

The venue is beautiful. It truly feels like walking through a museum, filled with artistic pieces and rich character. The owner clearly has great taste, and the space photographs wonderfully. However, I want to share an honest opinion about how my wife and I felt about our overall experience.

Organization and Communication:
Throughout planning, there were several walkthroughs we scheduled over email, only to arrive and find the venue team had forgotten why we were there. This lack of organization continued throughout the event. If you’re looking for a venue that values structure and consistency, this is not it.

Vendor Restrictions:
Be aware that the venue only works with a very limited list of caterers. If you want to bring your own, that will not be possible. We worked with Tastings, one of their approved vendors, and they were absolutely wonderful — the one bright spot in the process.

Music and Sound Issues:
The venue’s sound system was not functioning properly. During our first dance, the music was so quiet that guests could be heard talking over it. The DJ, without us asking, brought in an additional speaker because the venue’s equipment wasn’t working as expected. Outside speakers are not allowed, but couples should know that the built-in system is very low and unreliable.

Unprofessional Owner Presence:
The owner, Karen, was a constant and uncomfortable presence throughout the evening. Multiple guests commented on how unusual it was to see a venue owner so visibly involved, often interrupting and confronting us instead of coordinating quietly through our day-of planner. It made what should have been a joyful night stressful and awkward.

Service and Décor Issues:

After spending so much time, money, and effort to make our day special, it was incredibly disappointing to deal with so many avoidable issues — especially ones that required us and our guests to step in repeatedly.
